opus98.nome: Combate aéreo 3D do cinema mudo, P&B tingido
opus98.descricao_en: A three.js dogfight graded like a 1927 orthochromatic print: white skies, deep blacks, an amber tint, gate weave and scratches. Wings is remembered for aerial combat shot from cameras strapped to the planes, so most cameras here ride on the planes.
opus98.prompt_en: Smooth-shaded 3D graded as a silent-era orthochromatic print: high contrast, reds go black. Sky near-white, ground in readable mid-greys, deep blacks (25-35% of frame) only in silhouettes. Tint: blend whites half-way toward amber #FFCC80, so the sky is pale cream-amber, never solid orange; blacks stay black. Only the hero the story centres on keeps colour, whole figure at ~70% saturation (e.g. #D97757); every lamp, fire or other light source stays grey. 24 fps gate weave (±1 px), flicker (±5%), fine grain (±4%), 1-3 thin scratches, sparse dust, rounded corners, vignette; open on a 1 s iris. Signature shot: a camera rigged to something moving with the subject, rig in frame; then chase and POV. Cut every 2-3 s; white out through cloud, smoke or glare. Reference: William Wellman, *Wings* (1927). Avoid: motion blur, colour in the greys.

opus98.nome: Pôster art déco preto e dourado
opus98.descricao_en: An Art Deco revue poster in black, gold and silver: airbrushed gradients, a stepped proscenium, a chrome condenser mic. It is 1929 Broadway at the height of Deco, and the film where sound arrives, so rings of sound pour out of the mic.
opus98.prompt_en: Art Deco revue poster. Black lacquer ground; gold and silver from banded metallic gradients (3-5 hard bands); airbrush glows, sunbursts, ziggurat steps, streamlined curves; a stepped proscenium frame of gold lines and bulbs. Palette: ground #0A0908, gold #D6B560, highlight #F3E2A2, silver #BFC4C9; skin pale silver-cream; one saturated accent (e.g. #D97757) only on the hero the story centres on. Elongated Erté-style figures with real faces; fringe, sequins or feathers where the subject allows. Fine grain, glints, stars. Frontal symmetry, a central spotlight. Motion: chasing bulbs, a row of repeated elements (dancers, waves, columns) rippling toward the centre, rings radiating from the main sound or light source; slow pushes, cut on the music's beat (without music, every 2-3 s). References: A. M. Cassandre's posters, Erté's costumes. Avoid: flat yellow for metal, faceless figures, extra hues.

opus98.filme: All Quiet on the Western Front
opus98.nome: Xilogravura antiguerra à Kollwitz
opus98.descricao_en: A woodcut after Käthe Kollwitz: big masses of black, white knife-cut contours, rough grain, with Clawd printed from its own orange block. Kollwitz's German anti-war prints of 1921–22 come from the same war and the same grief as the film.
opus98.prompt_en: Expressionist woodcut after Käthe Kollwitz, *Krieg* (1921-22). 60-70% solid black; white contour cuts 1/300-1/150 of frame width separate forms; faces are white shapes with a few black features; hands large. Figures fill the frame, cropped by its edges. Each cut tapers in and out with chipped edges, is wider the nearer it sits to the light, in slightly uneven bundles. Ink #17130F on paper #E8DFCA; texture is only wood-grain streaks and under-inked speckle (±5%). One colour block (e.g. #D97757) only on the hero the story centres on, flat on its body or clothes, cuts over it; black stays 60%+. Light enters through one opening (window, cloud gap); lamps get a short ring of cuts. The ground under figures stays uncut black. Quiet motion (breathing, a small gesture); slow pans and push-ins. Avoid: grey fog or midtones, even striped hatching, gore.

opus98.nome: Panorama em sépia de 1889
opus98.descricao_en: A gold-toned albumen panorama of 1889: soft lens, a little pan blur, cream highlights and umber shadows, silver grain; only Clawd is hand-tinted. Cimarron opens on the 1889 land rush, so it is shot as a photograph of that year, keeping the chapter monochrome.
opus98.prompt_en: A moving 1880s gold-toned albumen photograph. Paint soft-edged flat shapes by brightness: main subjects dark (15-30%), ground 50-60%, sky about 90%; visible hatching and grass tufts (lines ~1/300 of frame width). Then print: grayscale, slight blur (~1/800 of frame width), a faint smear of three horizontal offset copies growing with camera speed, multiply cream #F2DCB4, lift blacks to umber #2E1C0F, blotchy development (±5%), vignette to #785634, per-frame grain (±4%), dust, scratches. Hand-tint only the hero the story centres on (e.g. #D97757) as transparent dye, mask feathered 2-3 px; lamps stay sepia. Wide panorama: the middle band packed with repeated small elements (figures, animals, vehicles; for a lone subject fences, posts, trees), no big plane dominating. Camera: one 4-5 s ease-out pull back from the hero to the panorama. Avoid: hard ink outlines, colour beyond the hero, a flat grey print.

opus98.nome: Saguão 3D em P&B prateado da MGM
opus98.descricao_en: A three.js model of the circular lobby, graded in MGM's silver black and white with Clawd's orange as the only colour. The film's best-known image is the shot straight down the well, galleries closing in rings, so the set is built around it.
opus98.prompt_en: A real 3D set, by default an Art Deco interior (marble, chrome, chandelier, glossy checkerboard floor); outdoors keep the real setting with glossy surfaces (wet pavement, still water) and symmetrical framing. Ambient occlusion, soft bloom; 1930s studio silver: about 40% deep black, glossy whites near 90%, no washed-out greys. Light falls in shafts from one high source. All neutral grey except the hero the story centres on (e.g. #D97757), at least 1/6 of frame height; warm lamps render white, bloom only around them. Grain (±3%), halation. Signature shot: eye-height wide into a deep symmetrical set, floor and ceiling in frame, floor reflections; then 4-6 s tracks; one overhead on rings, figures as chess pieces. Period figures (heads, hats, limbs) walk routes. References: art director Cedric Gibbons, cinematographer William Daniels. Avoid: walking in place, frame-filling abstract patterns, colour casts.

opus98.nome: Painel art nouveau à Mucha
opus98.descricao_en: A Mucha-style Art Nouveau panel: swelling brown outlines, pastel flats, a mosaic ground and a halo behind the central figure. Cavalcade opens on New Year's Eve 1899 with a family toasting the new century, so the halo is a clock striking twelve.
opus98.prompt_en: Alphonse Mucha colour lithograph. Brown contours #4B3326, about 1/250 of frame width, doubling on the shadow side (light from upper left), tapered ends; pastel flats, each with a hard-edged darker shadow tone. Palette: cream #F5ECD6 paper/sky, sage #A9B490 foliage/drapery, pale gold #CFA55A halo/ornament, rose #DBA49C skin/flowers; the hero the story centres on in one stronger accent (e.g. #D97757). Wide frame: figure and a big ring-filled halo in the middle third, arched panels either side, behind them a muted-teal (sage plus grey) square-tile mosaic; whiplash vines, local flowers; a bottom band of serif capitals in the user's language, 1/25 of frame height. No plain area over 1/8 of frame. Almond eyes, heavy lids; hair or cloth in three-tone strands. Litho grain, paper mottle, vignette. Slow sway; tilt down to the halo, pull back. Avoid: thin clean lines, saturated colour, empty backgrounds.

opus98.nome: Desenho "rubber hose" dos anos 30 em P&B
opus98.descricao_en: A 1934 black-and-white rubber-hose cartoon: thick-thin ink, pie-cut eyes, white gloves, cel shading over grey watercolour backgrounds, with film grain. It is the film's own year, and a road comedy gag suits cartoon timing.
opus98.prompt_en: Early-1930s black-and-white rubber-hose cartoon. Characters: noodle limbs, white gloves, pie-cut eyes, round heads; thick-thin ink #141414 (1/400-1/150 of frame width) swelling away from the light (default upper left); fills pure black and white plus at most one light grey for the hard shadow, gloss on blacks. Backgrounds stay mid-grey (30-80%), never pure black/white: graphite lines left in, grey watercolour washes with pooled edges and granulation, paper grain. Only the hero the story centres on has colour (e.g. #D97757): its whole body, or its one key prop if the hero is human. ±1 px gate weave, grain (±4%), flicker, scratches, dust. Actions anticipate, overshoot, settle: squash on landing, stretch on fast moves, eyes pop when surprised, a camera jolt on hits. References: Fleischer's Betty Boop shorts; Disney's Silly Symphonies backgrounds. Avoid: smooth vector lines, grey characters merging with the background.

opus98.nome: Carta náutica em gravura em cobre
opus98.descricao_en: An 18th-century Admiralty sea chart engraved in copperplate, with rhumb lines, compass roses, soundings and thin hand colour; the Bounty is a ship vignette on the sheet. The film is a voyage, so the whole film stays on the chart.
opus98.prompt_en: A late-18th-century copperplate map, default an Admiralty sea chart (inland: a survey map). Fine burin hatching and cross-hatching (lines ~1/1200 of frame width) give all tone; a minimum line width makes small detail darken, not vanish. Ink #1C1610 on laid paper #EFE3C4, light foxing, folds. Thin hand colour: water #9EBCBC along edges, land #B8C08C; the hero the story centres on (e.g. #D97757) is the one strong colour. Rhumb lines from 32-point roses, a graduated border, hachured hills, cartouche, one ornament (e.g. a sea monster), serif lettering. Put the action in an unboxed engraved vignette fading into the chart, filling 60-75% of frame height at the end of the move. Camera: one 5-6 s glide from the whole sheet into the vignette, chart still around it; a dotted route inks itself in. Avoid: cropping the paper, heavy washes, stiff figures.

opus98.nome: Palco 3D em P&B prateado, bolo de noiva
opus98.descricao_en: A three.js model of the revolving spiral 'wedding cake' stage in MGM's silver black and white: satin, chiffon and ostrich feathers against deep black, Clawd the only colour. The 175-step spiral of 'A Pretty Girl Is Like a Melody' is the film's famous set piece.
opus98.prompt_en: Real 3D stage spectacle in 1930s studio silver: the subject's world built as a revue set on a round tiered platform turning about 3° per second, draped and garlanded; its people become rows of costumed chorus figures with faces and arms. Costumes light satin grey, set mid-grey, pleated curtain backdrop darker, theatre deep black; whites below pure white. Soft front key; brighter rim lights edging satin and feathers near-white. Faint shafts, grain (±3%). All neutral grey except the hero the story centres on (e.g. #D97757); lamps render white. Signature shot: low medium along the tiers, figures 1/4-1/3 of frame height, the hero on the front tier. Then a 3 s curtain rise, a 10 s crane up to a level medium of the hero. Reference: Robert Z. Leonard, *The Great Ziegfeld* (1936). Avoid: flat lighting, faceless cones, fast spinning.

opus98.nome: Jornal em tipografia e gravura a traço
opus98.descricao_en: Letterpress newsprint with 1890s line engraving: a wood-type headline, dense columns of lead type, ink spread and under-inking on yellowed paper, figures in hatching. The film's best-known image is L'Aurore's 'J'Accuse…!' front page of 13 January 1898.
opus98.prompt_en: 1890s newspaper print. Set text as a sharp mask, then print: ~1 px blur and a noisy threshold for ink spread, ragged edges, under-inked patches, faint mirrored show-through. Page grammar: masthead, a wood-type headline across the width (~1/6 of frame height), 3-6 columns of small type in the user's language (~1/80 of frame height) flanking one large engraved picture. Wood-type letters are grained blocks. Everything pictured is a line engraving: hatching lines about 1/1000 of frame width, spaced 1/400, following the form, cross-hatching only in darks, heavier shadow-side contours, paler distance. Warm black #17130F on newsprint #E8E0CC; the hero the story centres on gets one accent plate (e.g. #D97757), offset 1-2 px. Motion: type blocks slam down, bounce and leave their print; one repeating mechanical motion, pages turning. Avoid: clean digital type, smooth grey shading, other colours.

opus98.filme: You Can't Take It with You
opus98.nome: Pôster serigráfico da WPA
opus98.descricao_en: A 1930s WPA silkscreen poster: six flat opaque inks, split-fountain gradients, slight misregistration on rag paper. The Federal Art Project posters of 1936–39 were American graphic design of the film's own years, and they keep it apart from No. 10's newsprint.
opus98.prompt_en: A 1936-39 WPA (Federal Art Project) silkscreen poster. Six opaque inks printed light to dark, each later screen cut away around lighter shapes (clouds, sun): cream #F0E2C0 for light, ochre #E0A842 and vermilion #C84A2A for sky and warm planes, teal #22686E for water and shade, the hero's own ink (e.g. #D97757, only on the hero the story centres on), brown keyline #322018 last. Shadows: a darker ink overprinted, never grey. Big areas get split-fountain blends: two inks in 2-3 coarse steps, the middle one their overprint. Screens 1-3 px off register; wandering stencil edges, squeegee streaks, warm rag-paper grain (±5%) on every flat. Figures fill 1/2-2/3 of frame height: big planes, crescent shadows, expressive faces. A bold capital title band, user's language. Slow pushes; screens pop in one by one. Avoid: halftone dots, smooth gradients, clean vector flats.

opus98.nome: Óleo empastado em Technicolor
opus98.descricao_en: Impasto oil with palette-knife slabs, ridged paint and Technicolor heat: skies burning from gold to blood red, red earth, black silhouettes. Gone with the Wind is where colour arrives in the film, so Tara at sunset is the first fully saturated frame.
opus98.prompt_en: Impasto oil in a 1939 Technicolor palette. Palette-knife slabs: long horizontal sky bands (1/15-1/6 of frame width long, about 1/60 tall), shorter strokes following form on land and figures, calm thin areas between; ridges lit from upper left, paint thickest in highlights, canvas weave where thin. Default sunset sky: wine #3A0912, red #A8241A, orange #F27A22, gold #FFD878; ground red-brown #6E2214; warm near-black silhouettes. The hero the story centres on stays a readable warm mid-tone (e.g. #D97757), never a silhouette. Strong backlight, gold rims; in close shots a warm side light on half the face and hands. Epic-poster composition: big dark silhouettes (trees, buildings, rocks, figures) on a low horizon. Lamps as painted flames. Camera: slow push on the wide, low push-in on the hero, crane up to a vista. Avoid: tiled same-size strokes, muddy browns, smooth gradients.

opus98.nome: Desenho gótico a carvão
opus98.descricao_en: Charcoal on toothed paper: velvet blacks, smudged greys, moonlight and mist lifted out with an eraser. Hitchcock's Rebecca is a black-and-white Gothic dream of a house in mist and then in flames, and charcoal can draw both.
opus98.prompt_en: Charcoal on toothed paper. Fine tooth (grain ~1/600 of frame width): light pressure catches only the peaks, heavy pressure fills the valleys. Grain only in midtones; velvet blacks, clean-paper lifts. Values: ~60% dark-to-mid grey, 15% deep black in the nearest foreground and largest masses, lights small. Charcoal #121111 on paper #EEECE7. Marks: broken vine lines, side-of-the-stick sweeps (1/60-1/30 of frame width) following form, hatching, finger smudges, eraser lifts for edges and glows; mist is horizontal streaks erased out of a toned area (as in William Kentridge's animated drawings). Only the hero the story centres on is in pastel (e.g. #D97757), laid fairly solid, tooth peeking through, outlined in charcoal; flames stay charcoal-and-paper. Moonlight from above; 2-3 fog bands drift at different speeds. Camera: slow subjective push, foreground parting. Avoid: digital noise, smooth digital glows, grey blacks, empty bright skies.

opus98.nome: Guache de vale galês
opus98.descricao_en: Opaque gouache in the 1941 poster's gold and green: solid colour masses, coal-black tips, Kyffin Williams' heavy dark hills and broken contours. Gouache keeps it apart from No. 3's woodcut; the scene is the colliers walking home down the valley, singing.
opus98.prompt_en: Opaque gouache after Welsh painter Kyffin Williams. Directional strokes 1/80-1/40 of frame width, 2-5 times as long, ragged, fully covering; broken dark dashes outline buildings, walls and ridges; dark hills flecked with lighter green or slate knife marks. Palette: sky and light pale gold #F1C565 (not mustard), fields green #86A03F, darks coal #1D1B1E, far hills and water slate #48505E, small accents yellow #F6CF2F, other colours mixed from these; the hero the story centres on #D97757, at least 1/8 of frame height. Fields and sky light (~60%), hills and buildings dark. Warm grade under 10%, vignette, grain. Default low late-afternoon side light: fields lit, ridges rim-lit. From high ground in true perspective, a path leading the eye down; small repeated buildings (or walls, rocks) stepping along slopes. Motion: looping smoke or cloud, a lateral track. Avoid: watercolour transparency, vector fills, mud.

opus98.nome: Litografia do front doméstico
tecnicas: Stone lithograph with crayon shadow plate
Frank Newbould and Abram Games WWII posters
opus98.descricao_en: A WWII British Home Front lithograph poster: flat brick red, deep green, cream and grey-blue, with a grainy crayon shadow plate. It fits the film's last scene, a village singing in its bombed church while Spitfires pass overhead.
opus98.prompt_en: A 1942 British wartime stone-lithograph poster. Simple, strong shapes from three plates, 1-3 px off register: a colour plate with all flat fills; a grey-blue crayon plate darkening every shadow with short slanted stone grain; a green-black key line about 1/500 of frame width around every shape, figures and clouds included. Palette by role: cream #EBDFC2 paper and highlights, grey-blue #8497A6 sky and shadow, brick red #A23F2D and deep green #34503F as accents, at most a quarter of the frame; browns and skin mixed from cream and brick; key #1E2422. Scenes may be full. Airbrushed skies; only the paper grain boils at 12 fps. Pale light bands, angled from the source, cancel the shadow plate. Figures stand frontally. Camera: slow drifts, a tilt up. References: Frank Newbould, Abram Games. Avoid: dot screens, clean vector edges, big saturated fields.

opus98.nome: Glamour de estúdio em preto e branco
opus98.descricao_en: The film's own look, Arthur Edeson's studio black-and-white, painted as a retouched glamour still: rich greys, soft-focus close-ups with catchlights, venetian-blind shadows, light shafts in smoke and fog. Clawd, as Rick, is the only colour.
opus98.prompt_en: 1940s Hollywood studio black-and-white, painted like a retouched glamour still. Forms: smooth airbrushed tone blocks. Faces: short key (light on the face's far side from camera; the near cheek in shadow, holding a Rembrandt triangle of light), two catchlights per eye. Slatted shadows from anything at hand (blinds, railings, branches) fall diagonally across surfaces; light shafts show only in smoke or fog. Values: 30-40% of the frame deep black, whites small and glowing; outdoor skies mid-dark. Grade: diffusion glow, an S-curve, fine grain (±3%), soft vignette, faint flicker; fog stays local. Only the hero the story centres on keeps colour, on its body or costume (e.g. #D97757); skin and lamps stay grey. Camera: a long glide, a push to a face, a pull-back into fog. References: cinematographer Arthur Edeson (*Casablanca*, Michael Curtiz, 1942). Avoid: flat lighting, grey haze, stiff busts.

opus98.nome: Vitral gótico iluminado por trás
opus98.descricao_en: Backlit Gothic stained glass: leaded pot-metal pieces with grisaille-painted faces, Chartres blue, ruby borders, and coloured light pooling on the church floor. Father O'Malley's boys' choir is set into the window under a gold star for 'Swinging on a Star'.
opus98.prompt_en: A backlit Gothic stained-glass window filling 80-90% of frame height and ~60% of width, neighbours glowing at edges. Every shape is cut glass: lightness varied ±8% per piece, streaks, seed bubbles, a brown edge mat, black lead (about 1/250 of frame width). Sky and empty ground: diamond quarries (about 1/30 of frame width); the border is ruby with beads. The main figure is at least half the window's height, in dark-brown grisaille line. Palette by role: background cobalt #1B3F9E, border ruby #B3121F, highlights gold #E3A526, lead #16161A; skin pale amber; scenery deep greens. Only the hero the story centres on is orange glass (e.g. #D97757). Bright glass blooms into the leads; coloured light spills onto floor and sill. Camera: tilt down, pan, settle on the pooled light. References: Chartres Cathedral; Harry Clarke. Avoid: flat fills, random cuts, dark empty wall.

opus98.nome: Arte com caracteres de máquina de escrever
opus98.descricao_en: The picture is typed: monospaced characters on a pica grid, grey built from character density and overstrikes, uneven ribbon ink on bond paper. Don Birnam lugs his typewriter to the pawnshops, so his own machine types the street; Clawd is struck in orange ribbon.
opus98.prompt_en: Type every image: one bold monospaced glyph per keystroke, fixed grid, cells 1/150 of frame width wide, twice as tall. Strike 85-95% of cells; bare paper only for highlights. Grey from a key ladder (light . : -, mid = + o, dark X # M); darks (about 30%) are overstrikes like M#. Shapes read as crisp-edged fields, clear silhouettes. Each material repeats its own keys (e.g. I H verticals, _| courses, ~ water). Signs stay legible. Uneven ribbon: half-inked strikes, a few keys always high or low. Paper #EBE6DA, ink #1D1C21; only the hero the story centres on, at least 1/3 of frame height, is struck in red-orange #D4704F, its shadow black. Hard sidelight casts long, crisp, dense shadows. The picture types itself within the first second, then holds. Reference: Paul Smith's typewriter art. Avoid: sparse frames, shapeless streaks.

opus98.filme: The Best Years of Our Lives
opus98.nome: Revista ilustrada em meio-tom
opus98.descricao_en: A 1946 picture-magazine news photo printed in coarse black halftone on coated stock, with the gutter fold and an overprinted caption. Deep-focus rows of stripped B-17s run to the horizon; Clawd is the only colour, on its own spot-orange plate.
opus98.prompt_en: Each frame is a 1946 picture-magazine photo spread. Render the scene as a grey photo (3D or painted): low sun, long shadows, deep focus (near and far both sharp). The photo bleeds across both pages, crossed by a soft vertical gutter crease. Print as a 45° black halftone, dot pitch about 1/250 of frame width, ink #1A1A1A on off-white coated stock #ECE6D8. A short black headline and caption sit in a quiet area. Only the hero the story centres on, at least 1/4 of frame height, prints on its own spot-orange plate (e.g. #D97757) at another angle, 2-3 px off, black only in its deepest shadows. Camera: walk in, push to a detail, pull back to reveal an open magazine. References: cinematographer Gregg Toland; *Life* post-war photo essays. Avoid: the gutter cutting the hero, coarse dots that break the photo.

opus98.nome: Ilustração de revista a grafite, anos 40
opus98.descricao_en: Graphite pencil in the manner of 1940s magazine illustration: construction lines, near-parallel hatching passes, rubbed darks and eraser lifts on toothy paper. The drawing builds itself around a polite refusal at a hotel desk; Clawd alone is in coloured pencil.
opus98.prompt_en: Graphite pencil like a 1940s magazine illustration, finished and controlled. The drawing builds in the first 1-1.5 s, then holds: faint perspective rays and head ovals, pressure-tapered contours (about 1/600 of frame width) overshooting at corners, then 1-4 near-parallel hatching passes (more for darker), about 1/300 of frame width apart, following the form, then rubbed tone and eraser lifts. The finished frame is toned nearly edge to edge: setting fully drawn in mid-greys, about 15% dark accents, only the outer tenth fading to loose margins. Paper #F2EEE5 with a light tooth; lead #2C2B2E. Only the hero the story centres on wears coloured pencil (e.g. #D97757) on its clothing; skin stays graphite. Faces carry the drama. Camera: a slow ease out, then cuts to close-ups. References: illustrators Al Parker and Robert Fawcett. Avoid: cross-hatch grids, scribbly sketching, a near-empty page.

opus98.nome: Castelo na névoa em foco profundo, 3D P&B
opus98.descricao_en: A real-time 3D Elsinore in high-contrast deep-focus black-and-white: volumetric fog, wet stone, swells breaking into lace foam, silver grain. It follows Olivier's castle, foggy battlements and sea rock; Clawd is the only colour, lifting Yorick's skull.
opus98.prompt_en: A real 3D scene in late-1940s deep-focus black-and-white. Built forms: bare masonry, block by block, bevelled, staggered (Romanesque arches only where the setting has them); wet surfaces dark and glossy. Soft overcast light, no hard shadows: dark masses against a silver sky. Low fog fills the lower third; the far background ends at 60-70% grey, the midground sharp; a bright patch behind cloud throws faint shafts. Water, if any: layered swells, lace foam, misty spray. Post: ambient occlusion, gentle bloom, high-contrast silver grade (true blacks, unclipped whites), grain (±3%), faint flicker. Only the hero the story centres on keeps its colour (e.g. #D97757); every light source stays grey. Camera: slow drift in, a track along a high edge, a low angle on the hero. Reference: Laurence Olivier, *Hamlet* (1948). Avoid: hard sunlit shadows, white-out fog, tiled textures.

opus98.nome: Cartaz de campanha em tipos de madeira
opus98.descricao_en: A Southern campaign poster in wood-type letterpress: red, blue and black ink on cream stock, wood grain in the solids, starved patches, misregistered formes and halftone portraits. It is Willie Stark's rally; Clawd is printed in a fourth, orange ink.
opus98.prompt_en: A letterpress poster from wood type and cuts. Three inks on cream stock #EEE3C7: blue #20488C (sky, water, shadow masses), red #C82C28 (warm surfaces, stripes), black #1E1B1E (outlines, type); only the hero the story centres on gets a spot ink (e.g. #D97757). Each ink 2-4 px off register; solids knock out the inks beneath, halftones overprint. Wood grain, pinholed starved patches, squeezed edges. Mid tones: coarse dots (about 1/200 of frame width), varied angles, on at most a third of the frame. Figures as linocuts: heavy outlines, gouged white lines, crescent shadows. Picture fills about 70%; short wood-type lines (about 1/10 of frame height, user's language) with offset shadows sit on banners and signs. Camera: small pushes, a lateral track, a bump on each strong beat (or every 2 s). Reference: Hatch Show Print. Avoid: busy grey mid-tones, perfect registration.

opus98.nome: Caricatura de linha única à Hirschfeld
opus98.descricao_en: Al Hirschfeld's Broadway caricature: one flowing ink line that swells and tapers, solid blacks against white, lots of empty paper, one exaggerated trait per person. The film is about the theatre, so its party is drawn as a theatre-page cartoon; Clawd is the only colour.
opus98.prompt_en: An Al Hirschfeld-style caricature. Lines are elastic, long and continuous, one stroke per contour: about 1/800 of frame width at the ends, swelling to 1/250 on curves. Dark clothing, hair and big objects go solid black; grey only as sparse parallel hatching. The setting is fully drawn in thin line, architecture, furniture and props in detail, white kept between objects: about 60% paper white, never an empty page. Push one trait per figure (a long neck, a big head). Paper #FBFAF6, ink #131012; only the hero the story centres on has its body or main garment filled flat with one colour (e.g. #D97757) instead of black. Lines write on within the first second, then hold; a short hand-lettered line may sit in the white. Camera: ease back, pan across, push in. Avoid: stiff limbs, stick figures, a bare setting.

opus98.nome: Balé em aquarela à Dufy
tecnicas: Loose ink line over offset colour
opus98.descricao_en: Raoul Dufy's watercolour: fast blue-black ink lines over big transparent patches of cobalt, lemon and rose that never line up with them. The film's closing ballet was designed after Dufy, so the Place de la Concorde and its dancers are painted his way.
opus98.prompt_en: Paint in Raoul Dufy's watercolour manner: colour first, line second, never aligned. Transparent washes (wet edges, pooled rims, granulation) cover most of the frame, 10-40% oversized, slid one way by about 1/30 of frame width: cobalt #2258CE for sky and water, lemon #FCE02E for light and ground, rose #EC3A7C for warm planes. Overlaps mix violet or green, never brown; keep the hero's wash off blue. Then draw the whole scene densely in quick, thin blue-black ink (about 1/700 of frame width) with flicked ends: buildings, windows, figures, extras; straight edges overshoot corners; trees and clouds as looped strings. Ink #1E1E3A; bare paper 20-30%, skin included. The hero the story centres on gets its own wash (e.g. #D97757). Figures bounce. Camera: small pushes, cuts on the beat (or every 2 s). Avoid: muddy colour, lines tracing the colour, sparse line.

opus98.nome: Litografia de circo à Strobridge

opus98.descricao_en: A Strobridge circus lithograph: flat chrome yellow, vermilion and cobalt with heavy black outlines, screened and slightly off register on grainy stone. DeMille's big top becomes a three-ring poster, with Clawd as the Great Sebastian making the poster's trapeze catch.
opus98.prompt_en: A circus chromolithograph after the Strobridge Lithographing Co. (c. 1890). Flat ink, heavy black outlines (about 1/300 of frame width), crescent shadows, light from upper left. Four stones: chrome yellow #F4C416, vermilion #D62C24, cobalt #1E4EA0, key black #181210 on warm cream paper #EBD9B4; overprints and tints give only orange, green, brown, tan, pale blue, grey. Solids print flat; screens (dots about 1/250 of frame width) only on gradients (sky, skin, ground), each stone at its own angle, 1-3 px off register, stone grain. The hero the story centres on is solid yellow under solid vermilion, a flat orange (e.g. #D97757). Exaggerated perspective, radial lines converging on the action, several actions at once; any crowd is tiny individual figures, though a lone figure works. Camera: tilt up, lateral dolly, cut on action. Avoid: off-palette colours, dot-only crowds, a screened, pinkish hero.

opus98.nome: Praia em P&B de alta luz
opus98.descricao_en: 1953 high-key black-and-white: hard sun, dark filtered sky, blown white foam, wet sand mirroring the sky, silver grain and halation. It stages the kiss in the surf at Halona Cove; Clawd, playing the bugle on the lava rock, is the only colour.
opus98.prompt_en: Early-1950s high-key black-and-white photography, painted in 2D to read as a photo: no outlines or flat fills, only soft gradients plus fine texture (sand, rock pitting, cloth). Values: about 70% of the frame above mid-grey; sky light-mid grey, one step below the bright clouds; deep blacks small. Default: hard midday sun, short crisp shadows; under other light keep the pale sky and bright values. Water, foam and mist blow out at the peaks, keeping lace detail; wet surfaces mirror the sky. Print finish: gentle S-curve, slightly soft lens, halation, fresh fine grain (±4%), light vignette, flicker. Only the hero the story centres on keeps colour, whole figure (e.g. #D97757), shaded photographically. Camera: tilt down from the sky, tight level frame, slow pull-back. Reference: cinematographer Burnett Guffey (*From Here to Eternity*). Avoid: low-key frames, white blanks, cartoon fills.

opus98.nome: Realismo social à Ben Shahn
opus98.descricao_en: Ben Shahn's social realism: a trembling, blotted ink line over flat tempera blocks laid slightly off the drawing, big hands and long working faces, restrained slate, brick and ochre. Shahn painted dockers and union halls, which is this film's world.
opus98.prompt_en: Ben Shahn's social-realist tempera. Ink lines (about 1/500 of frame width) jitter and wander, break each outline into two or three strokes, sometimes doubled by a fainter offset ghost (a blotted line). Flat tempera blocks sit 2-4 px off the line, rough-edged, dry-brush streaks (one brush wide, about 1/100 of frame width) over a third of each block; model form with a darker flat of the same hue. Palette by role: slate #768492 sky and cool areas, brick #9E4834 and ochre #C89852 ground, buildings, clothes, ink #1F1A1A, warm board #F0E9DA; skin pale ochre; other colours: these darkened or greyed. The hero the story centres on wears the one warm accent on its main garment (e.g. #D97757). Big heads and hands, long faces, heavy jaws, heavy clothes. Camera: short pushes, tilt up, close-up. Avoid: smooth gradients, clean closed outlines, cheerful colour.

opus98.nome: Cinescópio de 1955 numa TV de sala
opus98.descricao_en: A 1955 kinescope playing on a wood-cabinet TV in a warm Bronx living room: scanlines, phosphor glow, a rounded bulging screen, ghosting and snow, all black-and-white except Clawd. Marty began as a live 1953 TV play, so the film is shown as television.
opus98.prompt_en: A 1950s kinescope playing on a wood-cabinet television. Inside the screen: black-and-white with a cool phosphor tint (#DCE6EA whites), soft (half resolution, scaled up), halation, ghosting, tearing bands, a rolling hum bar, light snow, lifted blacks, flicker, grain; only the story's hero keeps its colour (e.g. #D97757), under the same artefacts. Tube: rounded corners, sides bowing outward, about 330 scanlines, glass reflections. Outside, a warm flat-illustrated living room (ochre wallpaper, wood, a table lamp), lit warm by the lamp; the screen casts a clear cold-blue glow on nearby walls. Signature shot: hold about 2 s with the TV filling 60% of the frame, then push through the glass (4-5 s) until the broadcast fills the frame, scanlines visible, then steady TV-studio mid shots. Reference: director Delbert Mann's live Philco Television Playhouse dramas. Avoid: heavy snow, a dull, evenly lit room.

opus98.nome: Desenho modernista UPA dos anos 50
opus98.descricao_en: A flat, geometric 1950s cartoon: colour blocks printed off their ink lines, broken outlines, crayon grain on cream paper. The film's own six-minute end-title animation was made by Saul Bass in this modernist style.
opus98.prompt_en: 1950s UPA modernist cartoon. Uneven ink lines #221C19 about 1/400 of frame width, sometimes broken; colour blocks sit about 1/300 of frame width off them, all one way. Objects are overlapping flat cut-out facets: a lit face and a shadow face one flat step (about 15%) darker. Pale aqua sky and cream paper #F2E9D3 cover most of the frame; mustard #E3A92B, teal #2B8C86, orange-red #D4452B are accents; sky, greens and slate blues are these mixed toward paper. Other times of day change only the sky colour. Crayon grain ±5% brightness everywhere, few flecks. Poster layout: one big graphic shape (a building or sun disc), angular outlined figures beside it. Light beams: flat pale wedges. Hard cuts every 1–2 s; slow parallax drift. After UPA, *Gerald McBoing-Boing* (1950); Saul Bass, *Around the World in 80 Days* titles (1956). Avoid: gradients, perfect registration, saturated colour everywhere.

opus98.filme: The Bridge on the River Kwai

opus98.descricao_en: A general-arrangement blueprint pinned to a drafting table: white lines on Prussian blue, folds, water stains, red-pencil revisions. The film is about a colonel obsessed with building a perfect bridge, so the bridge appears as his engineering drawing.
opus98.prompt_en: Cyanotype engineering blueprint. The sheet fills the frame (the walnut drafting table shows only on a pull-back): mottled Prussian-blue paper #143874, uneven exposure, a greenish over-exposed margin, creases, faint water stains. White lines #ECF4FF, sharp but printed: outlines about 1/600 of frame width, hatching and dimensions half that, broken where exposure was weak, a slight cyan bloom. Draw the subject densely in drafting grammar: elevations, sections, detail circles, dimension chains, hidden lines, single-stroke lettering, a title block. Notes and actions in red pencil #D63426, in the user's language. The one hero subject is the only hand-painted element, drawn above scale (at least 1/5 of frame height), opaque gouache in one warm hue (e.g. orange #D97757); nothing else is warm. Camera: layered parallax push-in; cut to detail views. Avoid: neon glow, clean digital blue, sparse sheets.

opus98.nome: Litografia Belle Époque à Lautrec
opus98.descricao_en: A Toulouse-Lautrec colour lithograph: flat poster colour, dry-brush contours, spattered ink instead of halftone, caricatured faces. Gigi's big moment is walking into Maxim's while all of Paris stares, and Lautrec drew exactly that Paris.
opus98.prompt_en: Belle Époque colour lithograph after Toulouse-Lautrec. Flat colour plates with wobbly edges; figures and main shapes outlined in a loaded brush (blunt start, swelling middle, split dry tail), about 1/250 of frame width. Crachis only on shadow sides, cast shadows and glows: 1–3 px dots at 1920×1080, sparse, under 15% of the frame, a darker step of the colour beneath. Large surfaces get grouped dry-brush streaks. Palette: yellow #F1C232, orange-red #E0602C, olive #6E7036, black #1D1A16 on cream stone-grained paper #EFE3C3, plus a muted bottle teal and greyed mauve; flesh is orange-red thinned with paper. Caricatured profiles with drawn faces; one large figure cropped by the frame edge in front. Flat, even light; shadows are flat plates. Camera: shallow parallax, a slow pan settling on a medium shot. Avoid: Mucha halos, smooth gradients, regular halftone, all-over speckle.

opus98.nome: Corrida de bigas 3D, épico em 65 mm
opus98.descricao_en: A fully procedural 3D Circus in widescreen-epic light: hard desert sun, dust, marble and gold, a Technicolor grade and 65mm grain. The chariot race is the film's most famous sequence, so the scene is the race, under the poster's golden colossus.
opus98.prompt_en: 1959 65mm widescreen epic built in 3D. Default: hard high sun (about 50°), short crisp shadows, cobalt sky fading to sandy white; under a low sun shadows stay hard but long, the sky turns amber. Marble, gilt, red granite and sandstone, with mouldings and fluted columns, never bare boxes. Warm sunlit haze mixes about 20% into mid-distance colours. Technicolor-print grade: warm, saturated, slightly contrasty, no clipping or bloom; fine grain (±3%), slight gate weave. Scale is the point: monumental architecture, statues and repeated elements fill the background, never empty. The one hero subject (e.g. orange #D97757) is the most saturated thing in frame; any repeated motion (stride, wheel, oar) keeps time with speed. Signature shot: low tracking beside the moving hero, 35–50 mm full-frame; then wide, top-down, close-up, low angle. Avoid: clean CG light, empty or primitive sets, overexposure.

opus98.nome: Títulos de linha à Saul Bass em P&B
opus98.nome_en: Saul Bass Line Titles in Black & White
opus98.descricao_en: Saul Bass's sliding white lines on black build the endless one-point-perspective office of the film's best-known shot, then fill with grey tones. Bass designed this film's titles; the only warm colour is Clawd and its key tag.
opus98.prompt_en: Saul Bass title lines turned into a set. A shot opens on black: thin white lines (about 1/800 of frame width) slide in and grow into a grid; by 2–3 s grey planes fill in and lights switch on row by row. Then hold the finished frame 3 s: mid-to-light grey, flat fills in 4–5 even steps from #140F0D to #F4F1E8, every shape outlined in dark line about 1/600 of frame width. Strict one-point perspective, centred vanishing point; identical elements repeat into depth (desks and people, or posts, lamps, windows). Figures: flat two-tone shapes. The only warm colour is orange-red #E2472A, for the one hero subject and one prop; all light stays white. Camera: a fast push to the hero, a hard cut to top-down, the grid becoming pattern. Avoid: sketchy lines, gradients, colour leaks, skewed perspective, unfilled wireframe.

opus98.descricao_en: A saturated, stage-like 3D block of the Upper West Side under a red-orange Technicolor sunset: red brick, zigzag fire escapes, rooftop water towers, posable dancers. It restages the aerial opening, the Jets' snaps and the poster's leap against the red sky.
opus98.prompt_en: Technicolor 3D stage set, like a 1960s studio musical. Simplified geometry, dense detail on every built surface (openings with sills, ledges, railings, ladders, strung lines); textured brick, plaster or rock, never plain. Theatrical light: a low warm sun rakes surfaces with long shadows; cool fill a quarter of the key. Painted sky of red-orange #E0481E, gold-edged cloud bands, violet only at the top edge; warm haze in the distance. The one hero subject in saturated orange #D97757, at least 1/6 of frame height, set against dark brick or given a black rim so it never melts into the sky. Puppet-like mannequin figures. Warm, saturated grade, fine grain (±3%). Signature shot: a low angle against the orange sky; then one continuous descent into the set and a ground-level push. Avoid: photoreal grime, violet-pink skies, plain walls, poses that pop.

opus98.nome: Guache de pôster épico à Terpning
opus98.descricao_en: Painterly epic-poster gouache with visible directional strokes and a hard warm–cool split: amber sand against cobalt sky. Lawrence of Arabia's original poster was painted by Howard Terpning in exactly this manner.
opus98.prompt_en: 1960s hand-painted epic film poster, gouache with oil highlights. Draw forms solidly, then paint: an opaque mid-tone base, directional strokes following each form (1/80–1/50 of frame width on large areas, smaller on faces and hands), soft-blended edges; model every form in three values; dry-brush only on dust, cloth and distant figures; sharp warm-cream highlights last on lit edges. Warm–cool contrast: cobalt sky #1F4D97 to pale blue #A9C3D6, warming to cream near a low sun; ground #EEC27A (any terrain); ochre-red #B56A33 for skin, earth and costume; violet #6C6394 for distant shadows. The hero centred and largest, a diagonal gesture, cloth streaming; smaller, looser figures may recede behind. Light board grain (±3%), warm vignette, haze. Motion: bounce, slow push to a low close-up, a whip pan out. Avoid: scratchy uniform hatching, flat digital fills, cold-only colour.

opus98.nome: Gravura satírica georgiana colorida à mão
opus98.descricao_en: A Georgian satirical print: Hogarth's swelling burin lines and directional hatching under bright Rowlandson-style hand colour brushed slightly off the line, plus a speech balloon. The film itself imitates Hogarth's 18th-century England.
opus98.prompt_en: Georgian satirical print: a copperplate engraving, hand-coloured. Brown-black line only: swelling burin outlines about 1/400 of frame width, heavier on the shadow side; hatching follows each form and covers every surface (spacing about 1/250 of frame width), cross-hatched in the darks, ruled on flat areas. Colour covers nearly the whole picture, clear but strong: washes spilling a few pixels off the line in claret #B3262E, brass #D8A93A, flesh #F0C4A4, slate blue #6D8AA6, warm ochre and umber on large surfaces. Sepia laid paper, foxing, plate mark, engraved border. Stage it like William Hogarth: big-nosed caricatures, bystanders or comic props and animals around the subject; one slanted handwritten speech balloon in the user's language. Camera: hold the full plate 2 s, whip in, glide to another detail, close-up. Avoid: even mechanical hatching, blank paper, colour exactly inside lines, muddy colour.

opus98.nome: Ilustração de moda à Bob Peak
opus98.descricao_en: Fast, dry-edged ink line with pink and magenta watercolour washes, splatter and edges fading to white paper. The original 1964 poster was Bob Peak's ink and pink; the scene is Cecil Beaton's black-and-white Ascot.
opus98.prompt_en: 1960s fashion illustration after Bob Peak. Fast ink line, thicker in turns, dry-brush tail, a flick off; 1/600–1/250 of frame width, thinning on tight curves. Solid black for dark clothing, hats and stripes; faces bare paper #FBF7F1. Loose, soft-edged watercolour pools, darker at drying edges: pink #EE84B2 as the main field, magenta #CE3076 for hot spots, rose #F4B2CC, a touch of plum #80285C; warm grey for secondary figures and shading; directional splatter. Settings are a few lines in these washes, not literal colour. opus98.nome: Voo 3D nos Alpes, livro de histórias
opus98.descricao_en: Storybook 3D over procedural Alps: saturated emerald, cobalt and snow white, sculpted ridges, cotton-ball cumulus and gusts running through the grass. It restages the helicopter opening that ends on Maria spinning on the hilltop.
opus98.prompt_en: Storybook 3D landscape in saturated 1960s widescreen colour: smooth sculpted forms, not low-poly or photoreal. Default light: bright sun high, a little behind the camera: emerald grass #3FA33A, cobalt sky #2F6FD0, clean white snow and clouds. Rounded ridges, snow lines following slope, grey-ochre rock bands, cloud shadows. Haze only on the farthest ridges, about 25% lilac. Cumulus are lit white cotton puffs. Knee-high grass and wildflowers fill the foreground, bending in gusts. A lower sun lengthens shadows and warms only cloud edges; other settings keep these colours. Camera: one continuous move: 0–2 s high flight, 2–4 s descent, then a low orbit through the grass around the subject (about 20° per second, subject about 1/4 of frame height). References: cinematographer Ted McCord (*The Sound of Music*, 1965); Miyazaki's meadows. Avoid: violet wash, needle peaks, grey photoreal rock, static grass.

opus98.nome: Retrato Tudor a óleo à Holbein
opus98.descricao_en: An Old Master oil portrait: smooth glazed modelling, fur painted hair by hair, velvet highlights, a gold chain link by link, varnish and craquelure. Holbein painted the real Thomas More in 1527, and this is his composition.
opus98.prompt_en: Oil portrait after Hans Holbein the Younger. Paint in layers: a toned underlayer, directional strokes following light and shadow, soft glazes, fine detail last; smooth finish, brushwork faint in background and fabric. Render each material: fur hair by hair, velvet folds with sharp light ridges, metal with two highlights per piece, wool and leather with soft nap. Any subject becomes a formal half-length sitter in its own clothes; its setting shows through a window or in an object it holds. Palette: deep green curtain #1F4A26, black #141113, velvet red #6E0C15, gold #B0801E, fur brown #3E2818; warm, fully modelled skin. Soft light from upper left. Signature shot: the portrait against the curtain; then material close-ups, a slow pull back into a dark room lit by warm pools. Warm varnish, light craquelure. Avoid: flat fills, hard digital edges, even light, unmodelled faces.

opus98.descricao_en: A three-ink Risograph print in deep blue, poster orange-red and fluorescent pink, with halftone, grain and misregistration; light is printed as less ink. It echoes the 1967 poster's orange heat field and black silhouettes.
opus98.prompt_en: Three-ink Risograph: orange-red #EC5032 as the dominant field (about 60%, with drip streaks), deep blue #162C76 for silhouettes and shadows, fluorescent pink #FF48B0 only for rims and halos, on warm paper #F7F2E7. Each ink is halftoned at its own angle, dots 1/300 of frame width, plates misregistered 2–4 px; grain, pinholes, slight boil. Knock orange out under blue silhouettes so they print pure blue; only the darkest accents overprint to near-black. Light is the absence of ink: beams, lamps and lit ground show bare paper, ringed in pink. Figures: blue silhouettes, pink rims; skin is 30–60% orange with a blue shadow step. opus98.prompt_en: Victorian toy paper theatre (Pollock's), all printed card: black lithographic outlines about 1/400 of frame width, sparse crayon hatching on one side of each piece; muted antique hand colouring: deep red #C8262C and dull gold #E0AB36 on proscenium and curtains (never bright yellow), blue #2F5A9A for costumes; scenery, sky, water and skin in greyed browns, greys and cream card #F4ECD6. Every cut-out keeps a white scissor margin (1/200 of frame width). Flats are parallel 2.5D layers in parallax, flat within each plane. Candle footlights throw each cut-out's shadow onto the scenery behind, about 1.5× enlarged, soft, flickering. Gilt proscenium, red drapes and painted audience boxes frame a stage opening 80–90% of frame width. Camera: slow push, lateral tracking, shaky close-ups; a final pull-back shows the dark room. Avoid: bright vector colour, true 3D depth, soft studio light, figures without margins.

opus98.prompt_en: Andy Warhol photo-silkscreen. Two plates: a high-contrast black halftone photograph at 45°, dots about 1/200 of frame width, few mid-tones; and hand-painted flat colour blocks underneath, offset about 1/100 of frame width with wobbly edges: taxi yellow #F3BE14, skin pink #F2A197, cream #EFE6CF, red #E2462B, on brushed silver paint #BABCC0 with a soft sheen. The one hero subject takes the strongest block colour. Uneven squeegee pressure: dots flood into blotches in places, drag into dry horizontal streaks and pinholes elsewhere, over faint canvas weave. Settings appear only as drained-to-silver prints in the repeat. Camera: handheld shake, a push in, flat frontal tableaux. Reference: Andy Warhol, *Double Elvis* (1963). opus98.prompt_en: 1940s US war-bond lithograph poster. Flat inks: red #C2342C, navy #213261, olive #5F5C31, khaki #B7975E, on fibrous, foxed cream #E6D5B3 paper. Three values per form (bare paper, flat ink, ink plus halftone), posterised in hard steps. Brown-black key line about 1/500 of frame width, printed last; shadows as coarse 45° halftone bands (dots about 1/150 of frame width) with crayon grain; colour plates offset about 1/600 of frame width.
